correctness.rationale: At a strict cyclic input, every mixed sign vector of adjacent differences is feasible: choose positive and negative increments of constant magnitude within each sign class with total zero. The piecewise-linear two-input bound follows by partitioning a joining segment; if a tie holds throughout the segment, perturb both endpoints generically and use continuity. Independently, the weighted ℓ¹ norm on zero-sum cyclic differences is generated by transfers e_a−e_b: match positive mass with negative mass to decompose each vector with exact additivity of weighted cost. Each transfer integrates to an arc indicator modulo a constant, so only arcs are needed for each linear selector. A strict base input can realize both prescribed choices on the two boundary sites, with a third edge enforcing a mixed sign pattern if needed. Adding an arbitrarily small multiple of the arc keeps the selector fixed, giving actual equality. For a singleton or its complement the output walls, if any, are one of the three L₁ pairs; otherwise the two walls shift independently left by zero or one site, giving exactly L₂. L₁≤1 forces w_{j−2}=w_j by cyclic iteration. On an even cycle the two smaller alternating edges attain the larger neighboring-weight ratio, which is also an upper bound on all wall shifts. This proves uniform-weight rigidity and the alternating formula. For w=(1,2,1,2), perturb (0,2,0,2) by ε(0,1,1,0), 0<ε<2; variation changes by 4ε for an input difference of variation 2ε, while L₁=4/3. Erosion follows by negation. The bundled program was inspected, not executed.
residual_risks: The proof is for positive edge weights and the forward pair on n≥3; general neighborhoods or path endpoints are not covered.

value.rationale: Weighted cyclic variation is a natural error metric on periodic signals; the two-input modulus, unlike one-input variation reduction, controls perturbations of a base signal. The exact formula identifies a separated-wall obstruction that changes the true norm already in a four-cycle, and classifies all weights for nonexpansion. The exact alternating case and actual attaining pairs make the distinction usable, not just a formal bound.
